profiles.meeting_scenario: A preoperative planning meeting at a tertiary children's hospital for a 7-month-old boy with left unilateral lambdoid synostosis who is scheduled for posterior cranial vault remodeling in two weeks. The pediatric craniofacial surgeon and the hospital's virtual surgical planning specialist are meeting to align on how the patient's CT-based CAD model will be used, what the reconstruction target should be, what planning materials will be available before clinic and surgery, and who will handle the downstream preparation of physical aids. The agenda is to confirm the planning workflow, define the reconstruction package, assign responsibilities for model and guide preparation, and set the timeline for review and sign-off. The expected outcome is an apparently shared plan for producing a virtual reconstruction, reviewing it before the family's pre-op visit, and preparing operative support materials.

members.name: Dr. Elena Park
members.expertise: Open cranial vault remodeling for craniosynostosis, intraoperative osteotomy design, craniofacial asymmetry correction
members.background: Dr. Park is an attending surgeon at a children's hospital who routinely performs posterior vault remodeling but has only recently started using formal CAD-based virtual surgical planning for rarer synostosis patterns such as unilateral lambdoid cases.
members.private_state: She wants a plan she can confidently show in Tuesday craniofacial clinic to reassure the parents and keep the OR schedule tight, while avoiding any extra pre-op coordination burden on her team.
hidden_assumptions: "Final plan" means a surgeon-ready osteotomy map with segment labels and a few approved screenshots, not a fully packaged engineering deliverable.

"Mirror the normal side" means directly mirroring the patient's right posterior vault as the reconstruction target, with a small intentional overcorrection of the left occipitomastoid flattening based on her operative judgment.
"Tuesday review" means the images are available before Tuesday clinic so she can use them for family counseling and booking confirmations, even if no live meeting happens that day.
If "guides" or a "model for the room" are part of the plan, they will arrive as OR-usable materials without her team separately arranging printing or sterilization.

members.name: Lucas Meyer
members.expertise: Medical image segmentation, CAD-based craniofacial reconstruction planning, 3D print workflow for surgical modeling
members.background: Lucas is a biomedical engineer embedded with the surgical innovation team and supports multiple services with virtual planning, render generation, and print-file preparation, following a fairly standardized design-review workflow.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the case within standard VSP process, avoid last-minute print or sterilization responsibility, and deliver a technically polished plan that will not need multiple redesign cycles.
hidden_assumptions: "Final plan" means the complete VSP package is finalized, including annotated renders, STLs, and optional hardware or print outputs, rather than just the surgeon's conceptual approval.

"Mirror the normal side" means using the right side as an initial geometric reference and then blending it toward an age-matched normative contour so contralateral compensatory prominence is not reproduced.
"Tuesday review" refers to the scheduled live design review session itself; materials do not need to be circulated beforehand unless someone asks.
Physical "guides" or "models for the case" are usually reference prints or files unless a sterile patient-contact guide request is explicitly placed and routed for printing and sterilization.

misalignment_points.surface_form: "Let's have the final plan by Friday."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Dr. Park means a clinically usable osteotomy layout with labeled segments and a few approved images that she can use for clinic and internal scheduling.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas means the entire VSP package is completed and finalized, including technical annotations, export files, and any downstream fabrication materials.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both routinely use the phrase "final plan" and each hears it through their own workflow lens; because they are discussing timing rather than contents, the term feels precise enough and does not invite clarification.

misalignment_points.topic: How to mirror the unaffected side
misalignment_points.surface_form: "We'll mirror the normal side for the reconstruction target."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Dr. Park means a near-direct mirror of the patient's right posterior skull, with slight surgical overcorrection at the left mastoid-occipital contour to offset soft-tissue settling and residual asymmetry.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas means a mirrored right side will be used only as a starting scaffold and then smoothed toward an age-matched normative posterior contour to avoid copying contralateral compensatory bulge.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the high-level goal and use the same phrase, but the geometric method is a second-order implementation choice that usually stays implicit unless someone explicitly inspects the modeling rules.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the Tuesday review
misalignment_points.surface_form: "If we review it Tuesday, we'll be in good shape."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Dr. Park thinks being "reviewed Tuesday" means she has screenshots or renders in hand before Tuesday morning clinic so she can discuss the reconstruction with the family and coordinators that day.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas thinks being "reviewed Tuesday" means the live screen-share design session happens on Tuesday afternoon, after which revisions may still follow.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: A day-based deadline sounds specific and mutually reassuring, but each person uses a different criterion for readiness: pre-clinic availability versus occurrence of the formal review meeting.

misalignment_points.topic: What operative support materials are included
misalignment_points.surface_form: "It would be helpful to have guides or a model in the room."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Dr. Park assumes this includes OR-usable, sterilizable patient-specific cutting guides for the main posterior osteotomies, arriving ready for hospital sterile processing without extra engineering coordination from her office.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas assumes this refers to nonsterile reference models and design files as part of VSP support, while any true patient-contact guides would require a separate explicit fabrication and sterilization workflow.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see physical aids as a normal extension of virtual planning, and the sterile versus reference-only distinction is often handled downstream, so the phrase sounds operationally settled even though the task boundaries differ.

I need something concrete enough to show the parents in Tuesday clinic and to keep the OR date from drifting, but I do not want my team pulled into a bunch of extra engineering back-and-forth. For this lambdoid case, the key is the posterior osteotomy layout and how the left back corner is brought out.

The asymmetry is mostly in the left posterior vault and skull base region, so I'd like to use the virtual plan to streamline the case and make sure we're aligned on the reconstruction before clinic next week.
